status_legend.VERIFIED_PRIMARY: Read from the primary or official text itself (NCC page, council DCP text in the JCE library)
status_legend.VERIFIED_SECONDARY: Read from a council guideline, government agency page or other document that quotes a standard; the owner must check against the standard
status_legend.UNVERIFIED: Could not be confirmed from an accessible primary or official source; do not rely on the value

_meta.topic: AS/NZS 2890.1 car parking and AS 2890.2 commercial vehicle design data

as_nzs_2890_1.value: Edition 2004 (with Amendment 1) is the current revision; a draft revision proposing larger bays was dropped (Standards Australia update, March 2026)
as_nzs_2890_1.note: Both the standard and its dimension tables are paywalled; a public preview shows front matter only (https://www.saiglobal.com/PDFTemp/Previews/OSH/as/as2000/2800/2890.1-2004(+A1).pdf).

as_2890_2.value: AS 2890.2:2018 (supersedes 2002); one council guide and one consultancy blog still cite 2002 values
as_2890_2.note: Values below come from council documents quoting the standard. Edition used by each is stated where known.

employee_parking_industrial.note: Consultancy blog links Class 1/1A with staff parking. Table 1.1 itself not retrieved.

visitor_customer_parking.value: User Class 2 (medium term) or 3 / 3A (short term, higher turnover)

council_practice_visitor_bay.clause: Cumberland DCP Parking and Loading s3.4 D3 note 2, p6

value.basis: B85 front door open service level; length 5.2 m B99 plus 0.2 m

standard_bay_2_4_by_5_4.clause: Appendix B Table B1, cl B4.2

extra_clearance_beside_wall_or_column.note: Where a wall, column, shrubs or landscaping adjoins a space.

front_overhang_length_note.value: Length may reduce to 4.8 m with a front overhang provision (blog)

value.note: Table B2 shows 5.4 m for one-way, but 90 degree aisles are always two-way so 5.8 m governs

aisle_90_degree.note: Aisle widths follow bay width, not one-way or two-way use (blog).

value.text: Aisle extends at least 1 m beyond the last bay; where a dead end cannot be avoided allow for forward exit

dead_end_aisle_extension.source_url: https://www.mltraffic.com.au/articles/as-2890-1-car-park-design-the-definitive-guide-to-australian-compliance-2026/ ; Melton Car Parking Guidelines 2015 p19 (dead end aisle length max six bays plus 1 m)

end_bay_next_to_wall_or_fence.note: Last space widened by 300 mm where bounded by a wall or fence. Council guideline.

b99_min_turn_radius_m.note: B85 min turn radius 5.8 m (same source).

tamworth_requirement.value: Manoeuvring areas must accommodate a B99 vehicle under AS2890.1
tamworth_requirement.source_url: Dropbox /_JCESite/NSW-Councils/_database/text/tamworth-regional-council/DCP/TRDCP-2010---Amendment-20.txt (extracted text of Tamworth Regional DCP 2010, Amendment No. 20; PDF /_JCESite/NSW-Councils/councils/tamworth-regional-council/DCP/TRDCP-2010---Amendment-20.pdf)

design_vehicles_as_2890_2._warning: Lengths and heights are from a council technical specification quoting AS 2890.2 Table. Turning radii were not available from any reliable source and conflict between sources; they are UNVERIFIED. Owner must read AS 2890.2:2018 Section 2 before use.

turning_radius_m.source_url: candidates: 8.25 (turn template notes https://dafinder.blob.core.windows.net/dadocuments/DOCs/TURNTEMPLATE-202443248-NOTES-01.pdf), 10.0 (mltraffic blog, which also gives a different SRV length of 8.8 m)

height_m.clause: Table 2 (turn template notes show 3.633 m; conflict)
Bayside Table 2 (turn template notes show 4.3 m)

length_m.source_url: https://www.mltraffic.com.au/articles/as-2890-2-explained-a-developers-guide-to-commercial-vehicle-facilities/ ; Griffith DCP No 20 cl 1.9.7 (semi-trailer dock depth 19.0 m)
length_m.note: Bayside lists 20.0 m; the 2002 edition is generally quoted as 19.0 m. Conflict.

tamworth_and_gunnedah_requirement.value: Traffic assessment must show safe on-site manoeuvring for the largest design vehicle; all vehicles must enter and exit in forward direction
tamworth_and_gunnedah_requirement.source_url: Dropbox /_JCESite/NSW-Councils/_database/text/tamworth-regional-council/DCP/TRDCP-2010---Amendment-20.txt (extracted text of Tamworth Regional DCP 2010, Amendment No. 20; PDF /_JCESite/NSW-Councils/councils/tamworth-regional-council/DCP/TRDCP-2010---Amendment-20.pdf) ; Dropbox /_JCESite/NSW-Councils/_database/text/gunnedah-shire-council/DCP/gsc-development-control-plan-2025-adopted-18-june-2025.txt (Gunnedah Shire Council DCP 2025, adopted 18/06/2025, Resolution 17.6/25)
tamworth_and_gunnedah_requirement.clause: Tamworth Step 3 Traffic and Access p40; Gunnedah DCP 2025 F.3(d) p58 and B.2(c),(d) p14

camden_design_vehicle_rule_example.value: GFA under 300 m2: MRV minimum; over 300 m2: HRV minimum; consider B-double
camden_design_vehicle_rule_example.note: Not a Tamworth or Gunnedah rule. Neither Tamworth nor Gunnedah DCP states a design vehicle by GFA; the tool should let the user choose.

griffith_dcp_loading_bay_minimums.note: Regional NSW council, written against AS 2890.2:2002.

value.width_m: 3.5 generally, up to 4.0 for larger vehicles

mltraffic_blog_loading_bay.note: Blog; page states internal inconsistency on edition.

as_2890_2_service_bay_dimensions_section.value: AS 2890.2 Section 4.2 Dimensions of service bays (values not retrievable; preview shows only the contents list)
